text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging alert: streaming/generate latency spike. p95 ~1.1s, p99 ~2.8s, 3rd-party-proxy timeouts increasing. SLO (p99 <= 2s) breached. Auto-created incident.
eng-oncall: on it. re-routing alerts to rotations. Checking dashboards now.
sam: I'm seeing a jump in tail latency correlated with a rise in `stream-chunk-delay` errors from the proxy. Logs show repeated `write timeout` to client sockets.
maya: customer-impact? any 500s?
liam: No 500s overall, but streaming sessions are stalling — clients report long pauses then resumed chunks. Non-streaming responses look fine.
charlotte: can you drop the p95/p99 graphs? need exact windows.
sam: p95 1.1s (baseline ~0.3s), p99 2.8s (baseline ~0.7s). Error rate of `stream-chunk-delay` jumped from 0.2% to 2.4% in last 10m.
eng-oncall: hypothesis: proxy buffering + client backpressure + kernel socket buffers. Also seeing increased retransmits on one egress host group.
ops-bot: quickcheck: `nginx/proxy-a` CPU 78%, `proxy-b` 35%. `proxy-a` shows many `upstream timed out` in access logs.
maya: which proxies are in the path for streaming? internal LB -> nginx edge -> svc-proxy -> runtime.
liam: suggest immediate mitigations: 1) increase proxy chunk timeout from 30s -> 60s for streaming route, 2) rollback new config that changed `proxy_buffering on` (if present), 3) route a small percent of traffic to region fallback.
charlotte: agree. Also enable a short-term mitigation: force chunk flush every N tokens at the runtime layer to avoid buffer accumulation.
sam: I'm pushing a config to lower continuous batch size and to flush small chunks more frequently. Pushing now.
eng-oncall: before that, can we toggle a feature-flag that sends non-streaming fallback for affected customers? avoids stalls while we triage.
liam: we can, but it must be opt-in per customer. who's on support rotation for affected accounts?
maya: Support reports two large customers saw degraded UX in last 15m — they open streamed transcripts to UI and saw pauses ~20-40s. No request-level 5xx.
charlotte: commit: start a 10% traffic shift to fallback (non-streaming) for public tier to reduce tail pressure. Ops, can you cut the route?
ops-bot: initiating rollout: `route-manager shift --service streaming --percent 10 --to non-streaming-fallback`
ops-bot: rollout step 1/3 successful.
sam: config applied: runtime now flushes every 256 tokens or 400ms, whichever comes first. Lowered batch window to 25ms.
liam: nginx config change staged: `proxy_read_timeout 60s; proxy_send_timeout 60s; proxy_buffering off` on streaming location. Applying to canary proxies first.
eng-oncall: canary proxies updated. Monitoring.
maya: metrics update?
charlotte: p99 dropped from 2.8s -> 1.7s on canary traffic. Global p99 trending down but still above SLO at 2.0s in some zones.
liam: good signal. Continue canary, then roll to remaining proxies.
incident-bot: automated note: incident severity escalated to sev2 due to SLO breach and customer UX impact.
sam: discovering root contributor: a recent kernel upgrade on proxy-a hosts changed the default TCP buffer autogrowth behavior — combined with a spike in slow-client connections it caused stalls.
liam: we have a list of affected hosts: proxy-a-3, proxy-a-5, proxy-a-9. I'm draining proxy-a-5 to mitigate. `kubectl drain node proxy-a-5 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
ops-bot: drain initiated for proxy-a-5.
charlotte: while drain completes, can we spin up replacement nodes with older kernel or conservative tcp_autotune settings?
sam: launching replacement nodes with `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_rmem='4096 87380 6291456'` and `tcp_wmem` lowered. Provisioning now.
eng-oncall: customer comms: support to draft note saying we are actively mitigating streaming stalls, some users may see temporary switch to non-streaming fallback. ETA for full recovery ~30-60m.
maya: sending email to affected customers and opening DMs for enterprise contacts.
liam: Ongoing: continuing proxy rollout. After full rollout to proxies, plan to revert traffic fallback.
eng-oncall: handoff: my rotation ends in 35m. I'll do a warm handoff to sam. Sam, check the canary dashboards and proxy error rates; if p99 < 2s for 15m, we start rollback of fallback.
sam: ack. I'll take over. leaving this thread pinned.
ops-bot: proxy rollout completed 12m after start. All proxies have `proxy_buffering off` and timeouts increased.
charlotte: metrics 10m after full rollout: global p99 1.45s, p95 0.9s, stream-chunk-delay error rate back to 0.3%. Looks stable.
incident-bot: automated note: SLO no longer breached. Continue monitoring 60m.
maya: follow-ups: schedule postmortem, include kernel change, telemetry gaps (need better socket metrics), and a playbook for streaming stalls.
liam: also add a smoke test that simulates slow-client backpressure for every rolling proxy upgrade.
sam: taking oncall handoff. My details: sam@redwood, oncall shift until 2026-03-15 04:00 UTC. Will update in 30m with final status.
charlotte: thanks team. quick retro notes: 1) quick mitigation (fallback) worked to reduce UX impact, 2) runtime flush change was low-risk and effective, 3) infra change (kernel) triggered unusual behavior — need pinning + canary for kernel updates.
eng-oncall: closing handoff. Sam, keep thread updated.
sam: will do. Final note for now: all key metrics returned to baseline; customer-impact mitigated. Creating incident postmortem ticket. :white_check_mark:
